item.title: 'Everyone's been bugging me': Trump to remove 10% duty on Irish whiskey
item.description: During the trophy presentation at the Irish Open, US President Donald Trump dropped a significant announcement: he plans to abolish the 10% tariff on Irish whiskey. This action responds to ongoing pleas from Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin and the golfing community. The Distilled Spirits Council of the United States views this as a welcomed change that will positively impact businesses and consumers in the upcoming holiday period.

item.title: Shot down over Iran, hunted for 50 hrs: How US fighter survived behind enemy lines
item.description: A US Air Force officer survived nearly fifty hours in Iran after his jet was shot down. Over ninety American service members deployed for one of the most complex rescue operations. The officer, injured, hid in Iran's desert while Iranian forces searched for him. US forces used bombers and drones to strike Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces nearby. This mission demonstrated the US commitment to recovering its personnel.

Clavicular Claims Cultural Impact: Ludwig backs 2026 nod; streamer says he streams less
item.description: Clavicular has responded after Ludwig named him among his five picks for Streamer of the Year 2026, alongside Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed, Stable Ronaldo and Jynxzi. Ludwig said Clavicular may have had the biggest cultural impact on the list, despite the choice potentially causing debate. Clavicular agreed, writing, "Easily the biggest impact on culture, but I don't stream enough recently." He also said he wants to create a real impact beyond streaming.

item.title: Former CIA official David Rush, found with 303 gold bars worth $40 million, reaches plea agreement
item.description: Federal prosecutors have reached a plea deal with David Rush's legal representatives, halting grand jury actions related to the stolen gold bars. Rush, previously associated with the CIA, now faces allegations linked to a fabricated classified program. The investigation revealed gold bars and luxury watches in his Virginia residence, raising significant concerns about classified information while circumventing protracted legal disputes.

item.title: Meet Henry Xie: 17-year-old student whose method made AI models more empathetic
item.description: A 17-year-old student created a groundbreaking training method for artificial intelligence that enhances communication skills in smaller AI models. This unique technique received impressive empathy ratings in various tests, paving the way for more advanced conversational capabilities in personal devices. By focusing on human-like interaction, the student's research pushes the boundaries of how we develop empathetic AI.

item.title: Palo Alto’s 500-foot horizontal levee reuses wastewater to restore marshes and test sea-rise defence
item.description: Palo Alto engineers have created a unique horizontal levee along Harbor Marsh. This innovative structure combines native plants and treated wastewater for coastal protection. The project aims to provide habitat and adapt shorelines to rising sea levels. Researchers are monitoring its performance as a pilot for future defenses. This living shoreline offers a new model for coastal resilience and ecosystem integration.

item.title: Since 2000, Marc Benioff and his wife bought 600 plus acres in Hawaii, only to donate 440 acres
item.description: Since 2000, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff and his wife, Lynne, have bought more than 600 acres in Hawaii worth nearly $100 million. They later donated 440 acres to support affordable housing on the Big Island. The Ouli Project will begin with 43 self-help homes for low- to moderate-income residents, along with parks and community spaces.

item.title: Reed Hastings took control of Powder Mountain with $100M in 2023; now he is spending $200M more
item.description: Reed Hastings is transforming Utah's Powder Mountain ski resort after a significant investment. He is combining public skiing access with an exclusive private residential community. New lifts and luxury amenities are being added to enhance both operations. This hybrid model aims to fund infrastructure improvements while preserving public access. Hastings believes this approach could offer a new blueprint for ski resorts.

item.title: In 1936, Memphis built Overton Park Shell for $14,000; 18 years later Elvis played...
item.description: Memphis's Overton Park Shell, a significant landmark built amidst the Great Depression, proudly celebrates its ninetieth anniversary. Known for hosting Elvis Presley's inaugural paid show in 1954, this venue escaped demolition thanks to community efforts. Now thriving as a vibrant music hub, it offers a lineup featuring both free and ticketed events, showcasing a blend of local and international talent throughout its anniversary season.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2016, NSW began fencing feral cats and foxes out of three reserves; 10 years later...
item.description: Thirteen native animal species have returned to New South Wales conservation reserves after a decade. These species had been locally extinct and are now breeding successfully within predator-proof fences. This conservation success is the result of a ten-year partnership involving government and scientific organizations. The state has now extended this vital conservation agreement for another ten years. Future efforts will focus on expanding these reintroductions beyond fenced areas.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Built in 1966, San Francisco's Empress of China closed in 2016; 10 years later it reopened its doors
item.description: The iconic Empress of China building in San Francisco has achieved community ownership after a decade-long effort. A coalition of six Asian American non-profits came together to acquire this historic site, aiming to convert it into a thriving arts and cultural campus. The restoration project aligns with broader economic and cultural revitalization goals, inviting future public sessions to influence its architectural evolution.
